title: tinyjs application configuration
description: Editor assistance for tinyjs.json. The CLI merges the current OS block over the root, then applies environment overrides. Unknown extension fields are allowed. Filesystem and effective configuration checks remain the CLI's responsibility.

$schema.description: Schema URI used by the editor; ignored by tinyjs.

override.description: Partial platform settings. Plain objects merge recursively; arrays and scalars replace root values. null clears a platform block.

name.description: Executable name. The CLI requires a truthy name after platform resolution.

title.description: What people see: window title, menu bar name, the .app folder (dist/<title>.app). Defaults to name.

id.description: Reverse-domain app id (com.yourcompany.myapp); defaults to com.example.<name>. Also keys the app's data folder, store, secrets and saved window positions — changing it after release starts users over.

version.description: Application version, x.y.z. Shown in About and app.info(); auto-update compares it; tinyjs publish requires it.

minTinyjsVersion.description: Oldest tinyjs version needed to run this project.

backend.description: Backend entry path relative to the project; omit for automatic entry discovery.

inject.description: Document-start JS or TS file, relative to the project.

icon.description: App icon path; defaults to assets/icon.png, then icon.png.

attribution.description: macOS: the credit line in the standard About panel (default "Made with tinyjs"). An assets/Credits.html or .rtf replaces it. Ignored on Windows and Linux.

helpBook.description: macOS help book folder inside assets/.

resources.description: Paths inside resources/. Omit to ship the whole folder; [] ships none.

executables.description: Paths inside executables/. Omit for automatic platform selection; [] ships none.

extras.description: Paths inside extras/: files for the person downloading (README, licence), shipped beside the app in the Windows/Linux folder and at the macOS dmg root, never inside the app. Omit to ship the folder's top level plus extras/<os>/; [] ships none.

executableEntitlements.description: macOS sidecar filename to codesign entitlement keys. The CLI verifies filenames against shipped executables.

signIdentity.description: macOS codesign identity; TINYJS_SIGN_IDENTITY takes precedence.

profile.description: notarytool keychain profile; TINYJS_NOTARY_PROFILE takes precedence.

keychain.description: File-based keychain path for notarytool, absolute or relative to the project. Omit, null or empty uses the data protection keychain. TINYJS_NOTARY_KEYCHAIN takes precedence.

activation.description: accessory: a menu-bar style app — no Dock icon (macOS) or taskbar button (Windows, Linux), and the window starts hidden. Default regular.

mainWindow.description: false starts a windowless agent. A remote url needs a main window.

url.description: Remote main page for a site wrapper, instead of a local frontend.

readAccess.description: macOS: let the page load local files outside its folder — true for the home folder, or one folder path. Windows and Linux already allow it.

downloads.description: What a download started by the page does: auto saves to Downloads (default), ask shows a save panel, deny refuses. Applies to every app; onDownload reports progress.

popups.description: What window.open / target=_blank do: external opens the default browser (default), window an app window keeping window.opener (sign-in popups), deny blocks. onWindowOpen can decide per popup.

contextMenu.description: false suppresses the webview's default context menu.

browserAccelerators.description: Windows: keep WebView2's own shortcuts (Ctrl+P, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+R…), off by default. Ignored elsewhere.

debug.description: Developer tools in a built app: true lets F12 open them (⌥⌘I on macOS too), "open" opens them with every window. tinyjs dev always has F12.

about.description: macOS: "menu" sends the About item to onMenu('about') / the page's menu event instead of the standard panel.

urlScheme.description: myapp:// links that open the app (onOpenUrl); a list registers several. Built apps only, never tinyjs dev.

fileExtensions.description: File extensions the app can open (onOpenFiles), without dots. Built apps only; on Windows it adds Open with, not the default.

openFolders.description: Folders can be opened with the app too (onOpenFiles). macOS and Linux, built apps only.

permissions.description: Camera, microphone, speech recognition and location, each with the reason shown to the user. macOS: the prompt text, and what lets the app ask at all. Linux: microphone/camera decide whether getUserMedia works. Windows: unused (WebView2 prompts itself). speechRecognition and location are macOS only.

location.description: macOS: lets the app ask for Location (permissions.request('location')), which tiny.system.wifi() needs for ssid/bssid on macOS 14+.

audioTap.description: Turns on tiny.audioTap: "app" (the app's own audio; true means the same) or "system". Without it start() fails with not-declared.

audioTapReason.description: macOS: the reason in the audio capture prompt. Default: "<title> reads audio output for metering and visualization."

windowPlacement.description: On Linux, prefer X11/XWayland for app-controlled window placement.

offscreenRescue.description: false disables automatic offscreen window recovery.

rememberWindows.description: Restore each window's position, size and maximized/fullscreen state per screen layout (main is shown once restored).

url.description: The manifest.json tinyjs publish wrote, where you host it. https:// only (http://localhost for testing).

auto.description: Automatic checks in built apps: a few seconds after launch, or that and then daily; a newer version fires onUpdateAvailable. Omit to check only when you call tiny.app.update.check().

publicKey.description: Base64 of a raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key, or a list of them (a signing key plus a backup), baked into the app. When set, updates require a manifest signed by one of the matching private keys (tinyjs publish reads it from TINYJS_UPDATE_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE); omit, null, "" or [] for unsigned updates. See https://tinyjs.app/docs/signed-updates.

dir.description: The plain page folder, served as-is; default src/frontend. A build with frontend.build ships dist instead.

build.description: Shell command to build the production frontend.

dist.description: Frontend build output folder; defaults to dist with a build hook.

dev.description: Shell command tinyjs dev starts — the dev server. Only used together with devUrl.

devUrl.description: The dev server's address; tinyjs dev waits for it, then loads it. Dev only — builds ship dist.

reload.description: false disables tinyjs's own frontend file watcher.

frame.description: false: no title bar or border (make your own with data-tiny-drag).

windowControls.description: Show all, none, or a list of close/minimize/maximize controls (zoom is an alias for maximize).

transparent.description: See-through window background. Windows: the main window only, and only when set here.

vibrancy.description: Blurred background material, such as hud, sidebar or popover; false for none. macOS; Windows 11 maps hud/popover/menu to Acrylic and others to Mica; Linux ignores it.

acceptsFirstMouse.description: macOS: a click on an inactive window also acts on what it hits.

menu.description: Windows and Linux: false hides this window's menu bar. macOS has one menu bar per app and ignores it.

panel.description: macOS: a non-activating panel. show() gives it the keyboard without activating the app, so it can open over a full-screen app (with setAllSpaces). Set here or in win.open; setChrome can't change it. Ignored on Windows and Linux.

windowControlsPos.description: macOS traffic-light coordinates; null or false restores the OS layout. Partial coordinates are allowed in platform overrides.

api.description: Which tiny calls pages may make — set it whenever the app loads a site you don't control. "all" / true: no limit; "none" / false: nothing; "wrapper": the site-wrapper preset; a list: only these; an object: { preset, enable, disable, origins }, where enable wins over disable and an enable list alone means only these. origins gives each site its own rules, first match wins. Anything unrecognised fails closed.

origins.description: Calling frame origin pattern to capability gate. Wildcards match any characters, including dots.
